item.title: A Motel With An Elevator. [Seeking Greenlight]: A Motel With An Elevator. [SEEKING GREENLIGHT]
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article, exploration logs, incident logs, and interview logs.

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is an elevator behind a motel that can take you to 6 non-existents floors with doors.

Genre: Horror and maybe a little bit of comedy and emotion.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: In 2010, The manager of Moonlight Shores went to the back motel to have a quick smoke break. While he was smoking, he noticed an elevator near him. He never noticed there was an elevator because he would always smoke at the back of the motel, so he entered the elevator out of curiosity and saw that there are only six buttons on the panel. He pressed on one of the buttons, and the elevator took him to a hallway full of rooms. He tried to open one of the doors but failed because it was locked. He tried using his management key to open it but failed again. As a last resort, he looked through the keyhole to see what was inside. He screamed and quickly ran back inside the elevator returning to our world. He then called the police and told them he saw a room that had eyeballs for walls and saw ordinary objects wrapped in human flesh. After investigation, the police contacted the Foundation, and then the Foundation purchased the property for testing.

D-personnel will be asked to open a few doors inside them and video-tape what they see or find along the way.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Each door has something special. One door could lead to a parallel-universe of earth, but it was taken over by an unknown species of animals. One door could lead you into a room that looks luxurious, but you stay in there long enough. Its looks fade away and you're left with a room that looks abandoned. One door can be just a room filled with clown paintings, and those paintings can make the person that looks at them laugh to death (literally). Who knows!

(Not all the doors are gonna lead you into a room, some may lead you outside of the motel, but it's a different version of Earth. I know I said this, but I just wanted to let you guys know, so you won't get confused.)

Additional Notes: Since all the doors are locked. I was thinking about using SCP-005 to help open the doors. I know people don't like the idea of older SCP cross-linking to the newer ones, but I kinda like it (biased btw). If you guys don't like this cross-link, I will change it!

item.title: Fireproof Rescue Dog: Re: Fireproof Rescue Dog
item.content:encoded:
Hello BreakerBreaker! lets take a look :)

+ show block
– hide block

Concept:

This SCP is a former SAR (Search and Rescue) dog that is completely unaffected by fire and smoke. When irritated, the dog is also able to raise its internal body temperature to an unnaturally high level, allowing it to essentially burn those who come into contact with it. Visually, the dog is a completely average looking dalmatian. Given that it was an SAR animal, the dog had a handler. However, the handler was entirely non-anomalous and the dog’s anomalous protection did not extend to them nor anything other than itself.

Overall I think this is solid, my one concern here is its purpose. While it has a strong motive, there doesn't seem to be much of a reason for it exist in the first place, which (at least for me) takes some of my focus away from the narrative, as I'm continually asking myself "why".

- that said, this is a fairly minor issue, as the narrative isn't centred around that aspect.

Narrative:

The central narrative of this SCP Article would be the history of the SCP’s life prior to containment. This would be told through SAR incident reports recovered by the Foundation, detailing calls the dog was used on and how the dog and it’s handler performed. The reports would be written by the dog’s handler and would detail their specific experiences working with the dog during the incident.

I mainly second Cybersqyd here.

The dog is contained by the Foundation after it gives several children second and third degree burns. This result is from the dog spitting on and biting the children when they irritated it.

This incident is what alerts the Foundation to the dog’s existence. The dog is subsequently contained, with it’s handler and any witnesses to the incident anesthetized.

The article would end several years after the dog is contained, with a researcher in charge of the animal noting its declining health and mental state. The researcher makes a request to their superiors to suggest the dog be used for SAR work once again, this time for the Foundation. This portion of the article is told through an email.

Overall this sounds fairly solid too, my only real question; why didn't the Foundation see if they could utilise the dog earlier? considering they know about its history, and its general behaviour. It sounds like they would've at least tried at some points to use it for something. Rather than (assumably), continually keeping it locked away.- what was their reason for doing so?

A lot of the narrative will be dependant on how its executed, and the concept overall is workable. With that in mind, here is your second GreenLight..

Cheers,

RED

item.title: Idea for Greenlight - Russian Nesting Souls: Idea for Greenlight - Russian Nesting Souls
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Standard layout + Incident/testing/interview logs

Elevator Pitch:
SCP-XXXX is a Russian nesting doll consisting of 3 layers. Upon opening the innermost doll; the object will activate. Upon activation, the 5 meter radius around the doll will be filled with a bright piercing light of no discernible origin for about 30 seconds. During this time, all individuals in area aside from the object's activator (henceforth SCP-XXXX-1) will immediately be vaporized. SCP-XXXX-1 will find themselves transfigured into one the now missing individuals, both in look and voice. The doll will now be embedded in the center of their chest with the front side protruding. Doll will now depict separate individual who was vaporized. Upon death or attempted removal of doll (which will cause instant heart failure), XXXX-1 will transfigure into individual depicted on doll, and the doll will change to depict a new individual. The entity will then come back to life. This process continues until all iterations have been cycled through and the entity will return to their original body; with the doll now depicting it's original marking. Any death or attempted removal after this point will result in permanent death at which object will dislodge itself. The object can speak telepathically to XXXX-1 and does so in a motherly Russian voice.

Central Narrative:
Through logs, the article will detail an incident during initial testing in which a D-class activated the object, resulting in the absorption of 2 researchers, an agent, a janitor, and another D-class. Further testing of object will be detailed as well as interviews with object will be noted. Ultimately, site directors decide object is safer contained in vessel as re-activation would require vessel be killed multiple times. Most knowledge of object is candidly provided by object itself in interviews. Object appears to have been created as a tool of war.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
I plan to weave a narrative of the D-class who has essentially became a living nesting doll, now with multiple "lives".

Additional Notes: I am aware of two other nesting doll SCP, so hopefully 3 isn't a crowd. The anomalous effects of the object should be fresh enough though.

item.title: Blood Rose: Re: Blood Rose
item.content:encoded:
+Show block
-hide block

This feels…kinda edgy and also a little insensitive towards folk who self harm;

I was trying to go for a slightly horrifying feeling; You're right, it does sound a little insensitive to anyone who self-harms. If it seems edgy because of that fact then maybe something else like, "it causes anyone to spontaneously bleed as they get nearer." Maybe the smell of the rose compels them to get closer, and then they start to bleed as they get nearer; and the longer the rose goes without blood, the more intoxicating and dangerous it becomes.

but I think the bigger issue is that the compulsion effect means you're removing a lot of the opportunity to explore why someone would choose to water the flower with blood.

You mention in the hook that the flower contains 'the history of all it's victims': maybe there's an interesting historical angle you could take this on then? Like, perhaps if the flower was considered a holy object or something and people worshipped it and were affected by it to a lesser extent and then gradually it got more powerful or something.

That's a really good idea, actually. I did think that this concept could go several different ways. Maybe a ritual someone was performing to bring someone else back to life, and it went wrong or something, and all the bodies in the hill were past victims. As for the historical part this whole thing could go back hundreds of years: every few years someone comes across the rose and dies, anything they had on them at the time tells how long ago it was. The DNA part might need some work too.

I read SCP-3597 and the way the containment process went might work for this, though it would be a bit different. It seemed based on a visual cognitohazard, whereas this is a smell cognitohazard.

So how about this instead:
The Foundation find a journal buried in the hill the rose is on. In it is the story of a man and his dead
lover. He tries to bring her back to life using a dark ritual. It yields a rose that reminds him of her, but he feels compelled to water it with human blood. He kills a few people for their blood before he starts to use his own blood to water it. He eventually goes insane and kills himself. But the rose still remains. Anyone who happens upon it is enamored by it's beauty and intoxicated by it's smell, and they end up bleeding to death when they try to get near it. So the foundation has a bit of trouble containing it, and they end up building a containment unit around it, and it grows into a massive thorn bush, but it stays contained.

I appreciate you feedback. Thank you for taking the time to look this all over.

item.title: Semi-Veil breaking Parawatch SCP idea: Re: Semi-Veil breaking Parawatch SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
Brought here on request, lets take a look.

Looking at the SCP itself, it seems fairly simple and straightforward. However, it may be a bit too simplistic? It falls under a thing that does a thing in my mind, a photo that when copied makes frogs appear. If that's the extent of what the SCP does, I suggest adding a bit more depth to it unless you can really pull off the comedy aspect of it. Even then, if you try that angle it may be wise to try and head down the route of a tale instead.

The narrative seems to have groundwork laid, but needs additional work. I'm really not sure how this frog picture almost breaks the veil as outlined. The Foundation lists Parawatch as a group that poses little threat to secrecy and the veil, and is purposefully left alone to misinform the public on the paranormal. So, I would suggest editing the threat to the veil either be more concrete or really play into the comedy aspect of the article. At the moment, I see how it could be humorous but pulling off a comedy article can be tough not to make it cliche. Either way, the idea still could use some work. You have a good start, but for me the idea is too simple and doesn't fit in with what Parawatch can do. Best of luck.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) Joke SCP - mind-influencing game code: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) Joke SCP - mind-influencing game code
item.content:encoded:
I'm not really a fan of an idea that boils actual addictions down to 'oh it's an anomaly', particularly ones that can be as quietly harmful to people as video game addictions can be.

Beyond this, the narrative feels…unfocussed? It kinda flits around various ideas: the behavioural patterns of the SCP, the way it affects players, the list of games it was part of; and it feels like these ideas never really come together to form a single, cohesive whole. It also feels like this could really do with a like…single affected player as the focus character, like, someone we can see slipping into worse and worse patterns of behaviour and whose plight is empathetic in a way that fills us with dread as we see them descend towards some final outcome that's terrible; but my concern is that the effect of the SCP is too compulsive for this to work well. That is to say: the SCP is effectively forcing them to become addicted, so there's no real like, choice or ability for them to like resist this or anything; whereas if the SCP was more…'seductive', then you can really like, have them be conflicted about whether they should stop and really give the narrative the conflict it needs that way.

I don't think it necessarily needs to be focussed in this specific manner; but it does feel like it all needs to come together in a way that makes it feel like this is telling a single, coherent story and it doesn't quite yet do that, for me.

item.title: SCP Concept: Guitar Hero: Re: SCP Concept: Guitar Hero
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Not really a fan of this as a whole. It feels…too much like a generic murder monster withy a lot of additional complexity that just, isn't very interesting to me; which isn't helped by the central narrative section just expanding more on what the SCP does. What I really want to see out of a pitch like this is an indication you've considered how you can explore what the SCP does in an interesting way, or like have built up some kind of story about the SCP and the Foundation's interactions with it that really emphasises why it's interesting to read about.

As an aside, murder monsters aren't inherently a bad idea to write about as a SCP; but they do present challenges to writing. Namely, you aren't trying to write a DnD Monster Manual style entry, and danger alone isn't interesting; so you have to figure out how you can make the danger feel interesting. Often, this is easiest by putting characters the reader cares about in danger (even in a very stripped down way e.g. SCP-3794, or providing clear stakes to the danger and having the threat be like, present. It's also possible to make it work if the danger is sufficiently interesting alone: something like SCP-5852 is a great example of that; where the core is very simple but the threat is effective nevertheless.

I think SCP-XXXX-ɑ is the best example of my issue with this: rather than relying on the user of the guitar being like 'wow I'm great at this I have to keep playing this', you've added a chemical it emits that basically forces people to keep playing it; and it feels like added complexity that doesn't actually make this more interesting. In general: it's a lot more interesting when people choose to do things instead of being forced to by a SCP because the agency that choosing grants allows you to really explore why someone would choose to do it and the conflict that choosing to continue doing something even once you begin to see the dangerous effects come in creates.

This isn't to say that's the only issue: the issue with this pitch at it's core is that instead of keeping the anomaly simple and doing something interesting with it, you've extended it's behaviour and the range of anomalous things it can do in an attempt at making it more interesting. My general advice for anomaly design is 'you should be able to describe what the anomaly does fully in one sentence': it doesn't apply always, but severely limiting the scope of the concept like that allows you to really focus on why the anomaly is interesting and how it's effects affect the world at large in an easier way.
